explicit_propositions.text: I returned from a sabbatical after several weeks off.
I deeply enjoyed my time away and found it spiritually enriching.
Spending time with the Lord is time well spent and beneficial for personal reflection.
The Bible describes Scripture as a mirror for self-examination.
My family chose to attend church at Oakwood during my sabbatical despite having no duties.
Our church has experienced salvations and baptisms during my absence.
Coronavirus has disrupted travel plans and caused significant lifestyle changes.
God remains good, faithful, and actively working in individuals and communities.
Time spent with God—through reading Scripture, prayer, and devotion—is valuable and transformative.
The Church is described in Scripture as the gathering of God’s called-out ones (ekklesia).

assumptions.text: Spiritual growth requires intentional withdrawal from routine responsibilities.
Personal transformation is possible through sustained engagement with Scripture and prayer.
The local church community possesses unique spiritual value that surpasses larger or trendier congregations.
Disagreements over public health measures like mask-wearing should not fracture fellowship among believers.
Diversity in individual responses to crisis reflects sincere, biblically grounded intentions rather than moral failure.
The ultimate purpose of the Church is to be the visible expression of Christ’s presence in the world.
Divine sovereignty renders human crises—including pandemics—inconsequential to God’s overarching plan.
Emotional and spiritual distress during sabbatical indicates genuine spiritual work is underway.
Leadership continuity during absence is dependent on volunteer dedication and collective commitment.
A public invitation to respond to the gospel carries divine urgency and potential for conversion.
